name: Transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty

card.summary: Lower-eyelid surgery through an incision inside the lid, so there is no outer scar, used to remove or reposition under-eye fat bags.
card.aka: Transconjunctival eye bag removal, scarless lower blepharoplasty, lower lid fat repositioning
card.note: Best suited to fat bags without much excess skin; skin laxity may need a separate procedure.

quick.overview:
In transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty the surgeon works through a cut on the inner surface of the lower eyelid, which leaves no visible external scar. It is used to remove or move the fat that bulges as under-eye bags and to smooth the lid-cheek transition.

It is an established surgical technique described in plastic-surgery literature, including combinations with fat grafting and other steps. Published support comes largely from surgeon case series rather than randomized trials.
quick.mechanism: Orbital fat is either removed or repositioned along the infraorbital rim to fill the tear trough hollow. Because there is no skin incision, it is generally described as suitable when there is little or no excess skin.
quick.risks: Swelling and bruising are common and usually settle over several weeks. Eyelid malposition is a recognized complication of lower blepharoplasty in general, and surgeons sometimes add a canthopexy or canthoplasty to reduce that risk. It is a surgical procedure done under anesthesia by qualified surgeons.

lead: Transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty is a form of lower-eyelid surgery in which the incision is made on the inner surface of the eyelid, leaving no external scar [1]. It is used to remove or reposition the orbital fat that produces under-eye bags and tear trough hollowing.

Surgical descriptions state that it suits patients with minimal or no excess skin, whereas a transcutaneous incision just below the lashes is typically used when significant skin laxity needs to be addressed [1]. Where skin laxity coexists, an additional procedure may be needed [1].

In the plastic-surgery literature the technique is described alone and in combination with fat grafting, including stromal vascular fraction gel, and with other steps tailored to specific lower-eyelid deformity types [2][3].

paras: Lower blepharoplasty is generally performed by one of two routes. The transcutaneous approach uses an incision just below the lashes and permits skin excision, while the transconjunctival approach goes through the inner lid [1]. Orbital fat can be taken out or redistributed along the infraorbital rim to smooth the lower eyelid-cheek transition and address tear trough deformity [1].

Blepharoplasty has a long history: the first-century Roman writer Celsus described skin excision to relax the eyelids, and the term itself was coined by Karl Ferdinand von Graefe in 1818 for the repair of cancer-related eyelid defects [1].

A study of fat grafting for facial rejuvenation using stromal vascular fraction gel reported using the gel for eye bag and tear trough deformity, alone or combined with transconjunctival eye bag removal, and noted high patient satisfaction [2].

A report on 183 patients with four types of lower eyelid deformity in Asian patients described a combination of three-step lower blepharoplasty tailored to the deformity type [3]. Both are surgeon-reported series rather than randomized comparisons.
Swelling and bruising are common after blepharoplasty and usually resolve over several weeks [1]. Canthopexy or canthoplasty may reduce the risk of postoperative eyelid malposition [1].
